question: As the owner, I want every customer who is sent a code to be readable at the window, so that nobody holding a valid code is turned away. About one code in seven is missed by the tablet's Scan from photo today. Which way do we go: fix the photo scan then land both cards, check the truck's tablet first, land the code as built, or have the server refuse unreadable codes?
proposal: Check the truck's tablet first, then decide: the owner photo-scans 16 sample codes on the real tablet before a night is spent on a fix

votes.note: A customer holding a valid code turned away at the window is the product failing at its point of use; which fix is owed depends on what the real tablet does
Activity E is the milestone's last close-bar work; the check costs ten attended minutes and delays it by at least a night
The lab figure is for the server's exact image on a browser with no built-in detector; the reviewer showed a resampled image changes the outcome, so the real device is the missing measurement

cited.statement: A capability milestone is dev complete only when the capability runs persistently in the operator's environment and the operator has personally seen it work at the app surface. Demo scripts, card counts, KR grades and closeouts do not substitute; at least one KR must measure the operator-run proof directly, and the milestone may not close without that recorded line.
cited.fit: Dev complete means the operator ran it in their environment: the truck's tablet is that environment, and the lab number does not substitute for seeing it there

cited.statement: Every async failure a crew member can hit (media load, data fetch, upload) has three parts: a visible error state naming what happened in crew language, a Retry affordance, and an authority override path (e.g. manager marks a training step watched) that unblocks the flow when retry cannot. Nobody gets silently stranded mid-task on a phone in a truck.
cited.fit: Failures are loud, retryable and overridable: a code that never reads leaves the crew a retry that cannot work, so the size of that failure on the real device has to be known before codes go out

weighing: Both adopted preferences point the same way: measure at the surface the crew uses before shipping or sizing the fix. Neither settles which fix follows, so the choice stays the operator's.
reasons: role pm cast an unrecognized severity "high" (want low, medium, top)
top-severity questions are the operator's — no number of citations clears them
